question: Should CodexBar automatically discover DeepSeek bearer sessions from Chrome local storage, and if so must that capability be implemented through a shared browser host API rather than provider-owned browser code?
rationale: The choice determines CodexBar’s reusable consent, credential-handling, and browser-access boundary; implementation quality alone cannot establish that policy.

options.title: Add a shared host API
options.body: Move scoped Chrome local-storage discovery and validation behind a reusable host capability, then keep the DeepSeek profile picker as its consumer.

options.title: Retain explicit token configuration
options.body: Remove automatic local-storage discovery and continue supporting detailed usage through the established explicit Platform-token path.

options.title: Accept provider-owned discovery
options.body: Merge the direct importer while explicitly accepting that individual providers may implement browser credential extraction and consent behavior.

recommendation.title: Add a shared host API
recommendation.body: Move scoped Chrome local-storage discovery and validation behind a reusable host capability, then keep the DeepSeek profile picker as its consumer.

likelyOwner.reason: The current DeepSeek web-session implementation was landed through this ownership trail, and this decision affects repository-wide provider architecture.
